parsed.explanation: No trans-specific statute, targeting, facility rule or visitor case is documented, so severity is not the 0.15 tier. But in this thin-data record same-sex intimacy is criminalised under both operative frameworks (6 months-3 years; up to 3 years), with detention/court operation documented and camp officials reported holding people on homosexuality charges. Social framing is hostile - same-sex relations read as foreign, most residents Muslim - and a refugee-aid body reports no protection against discrimination or violence. Under rubric rules 2, 13 and 23, a secondary sexuality statute in a thin, non-accepting, no-recourse setting cannot be treated as dead-letter; extrapolated risk is high, though unproven as a trans-specific campaign.

entry_documents.interaction: No documented document or marker practice; any outing at a checkpoint would meet the criminalised frameworks described elsewhere.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: administering-state penalty 6 months-3 years; movement penalty up to 3 years; camp officials reported holding prisoners on homosexuality charges in 2009; administering courts/detention operated in a 2005 political trial.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Which framework applies depends on part of territory; a trans visitor read as same-sex under birth-sex status or in such a relationship could face detention under either.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented: same-sex criminalised under both frameworks for decades per 2017 listing; constitutional silence is not decriminalisation; no statute decriminalises; social reading as foreign phenomenon.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No trans-specific protection documented; 2010 diplomatic statement is a position, not law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: No trans statute documented, so application to a trans person by birth-sex reading is uncertain, but criminalisation provides a documented police/camp lever in principle.

minors_guardians.interaction: No age-specific rule documented; a guardian's outing/detention exposure would be as for an adult, with no documented child-specific protection.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans violence documented; refugee-aid body states no protection for LGBTQ people against discrimination or violence; social hostility framing documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of protection matters if outed, but no documented trans-specific violence rate or police response to trans victims.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Documented absence of protection mechanism; document, facilities, care and trans-application questions entirely undocumented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknowns do not resolve to safety in thin data; structural extrapolation from dual criminalisation and no recourse drives rating.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier: documented criminal detention lever and no effective recourse make outing consequential, though this dossier lacks the documented routine police stops/extortion of foreign travellers in 0.35-C, so it is not clearly below it.

Materially lower: 0.65-C has documented traditional acceptance, no recent enforcement of dead-letter law and court compensation; this dossier has hostile foreign-framing, no acceptance, no remedy, and criminalisation under both frameworks.

Higher: 0.15-A documents a trans-presentation offence, repeated convictions and custody assaults; here no trans-specific offence or trans case is documented and penalty is for same-sex conduct, a secondary factor under rubric rule 2.
Lower: 0.55-B has repeated service hostility but mediators, readmission, refunds and a conviction; here no remedy, protection or service evidence is documented at all.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: visiting either part remains inside a same-sex prohibition, administered by operating courts/detention in the administered area and camp officials in exile camps. No trans-specific exposure is proven, but no acceptance, protection or remedy offsets the documented criminalisation and hostile social framing. If outed - especially in a relationship read as same-sex - the traveller faces investigation, detention and up to 3 years, with documented absence of protection. That combination, in thin data, places risk in the high-risk band, below documented trans-targeting regimes but well below acceptance-with-remedy regimes.
